MBLB Chicago Has Moved Into a New Office!
MBLB Chicago Has Moved Into a New Office!
October 2, 2026
By
MBLB News
Mouledoux, Bland, Legrand & Brackett is excited to announce that our Chicago team has moved into a new office at 29 N. Wacker Drive. Same city, different building.
Managing Member, Alan Brackett said, “We’re excited to establish a larger office to accommodate our team in Chicago. What started as three attorneys has now grown to eleven, and we wanted to create a professional space for our team and plan for continued expansion. The office has a great location and will serve us well for the next several years.”
The new office embraces a more contemporary working style and offers a mix of private and collaborative areas.
MBLB expanded to Chicago in August 2024. The office is focused on the defense of employers and insurance carriers for claims arising under the Defense Base Act. The firm handles DBA claims nationwide, so having an office in Chicago dedicated to this practice area has helped the firm expand its influence and reach.

Ogletree Deakins Expands Chicago Office with Three Attorneys, Including Shareholder Christina Wernick
Ogletree Deakins Expands Chicago Office with Three Attorneys, Including Shareholder Christina Wernick
October 26, 2026
|   
                    Press Release
CHICAGO – October 26, 2026 – Ogletree Deakins, one of the largest labor and employment law firms representing management, is pleased to welcome three attorneys from Laner Muchin Ltd. to the firm’s
Chicago
office: Christina Wernick as a shareholder, Megan Wilkes as of counsel, and Emily Chramiec as an associate.
Christina Wernick is a labor and employment attorney with more than 20 years of legal experience whose practice focuses on traditional labor and prevailing wage laws, including a particular emphasis on the construction industry. She advises and counsels management on collective bargaining negotiations, grievance and arbitration proceedings, and jurisdictional disputes, and she represents companies in multiemployer bargaining and in federal and state courts. Wernick also advises on due diligence for unionized asset and stock transactions, including bargaining effects and mitigation of withdrawal liability.
In addition, Wernick counsels hotels and restaurants, nonprofit organizations, municipalities, and other public entities navigating labor issues across different legal frameworks. She was recognized in the 2026 edition of
The Best Lawyers in America
®
guide for Employment Law – Management and included as a Notable Leader in Employment and Labor Law by Crain’s Chicago Business in 2023. Wernick earned her J.D. from DePaul University College of Law and her B.A.,
cum laude
, from The Ohio State University.
“Christina, Megan, and Emily each add experience that our Chicago clients will benefit from right away,” said
Jennifer Colvin
, office managing shareholder in Chicago. “Collectively, they provide business leaders with a broad range of labor and employment support, handling everything from collective bargaining and prevailing wage matters to discrimination claims, which complements our team nicely and strengthens our service offering for employers across Illinois.”
“Employers need labor counsel who understands the realities of running their business, not just the impact of the law,” Wernick said. “Throughout my career, I’ve focused my practice on giving that kind of practical, hands-on guidance, whether at the bargaining table, on site, working through a labor dispute, or in the middle of a deal. My clients’ projects and workforces have never stopped at the Illinois border, and Ogletree Deakins’ national platform and deep labor bench create a tremendous opportunity to build on that work and continue delivering responsive, business-focused advice. I’m excited to join the firm alongside Megan and Emily, whose versatile skill sets will make an immediate impact for the team and our clients.”
Megan Wilkes has more than 12 years of experience representing management in grievance actions and prevailing wage matters. She interprets and negotiates collective bargaining agreements, including project labor agreements, analyzes jurisdictional disputes, and handles ERISA audit and collection actions. She also defends employers in civil litigation, including employment discrimination and retaliation claims. She earned her J.D. from the University of Illinois Chicago School of Law and her B.A. from DePaul University.
Emily Chramiec handles a wide variety of labor and employment law matters, with a focus on discrimination. She earned her J.D. from Chicago-Kent College of Law with a certificate in labor and employment law and her B.A. from Loyola University Chicago. While in law school, she was a member of the Moot Court Honor Society and a student editor for the Employee Rights & Employment Policy Journal, and she received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award in Employment Discrimination.
The Chicago team continues to grow strategically, as the office has added 11 lawyers this year already. This reflects a larger growth strategy at Ogletree Deakins, which welcomed more than 30 shareholders to the firm in 2026 across its international footprint.
About Ogletree Deakins
With more than 1,200 attorneys in 62 offices worldwide, Ogletree Deakins is one of the largest labor and employment law firms representing management. We handle all types of employment-related legal matters, including traditional labor and employment, workplace safety, employee benefits, and business immigration matters. Guided by our
Client Pledge
, we focus on understanding clients’ business and objectives, collaborating and anticipating needs, harnessing technology and innovation, communicating effectively, and providing quality representation with exceptional value.

Ogletree Deakins Expands Chicago Office with Three Attorneys, Including Shareholder Christina Wernick
Ogletree Deakins Expands Chicago Office with Three Attorneys, Including Shareholder Christina Wernick
October 26, 2026
|   
                    Press Release
CHICAGO – October 26, 2026 – Ogletree Deakins, one of the largest labor and employment law firms representing management, is pleased to welcome three attorneys from Laner Muchin Ltd. to the firm’s
Chicago
office: Christina Wernick as a shareholder, Megan Wilkes as of counsel, and Emily Chramiec as an associate.
Christina Wernick is a labor and employment attorney with more than 20 years of legal experience whose practice focuses on traditional labor and prevailing wage laws, including a particular emphasis on the construction industry. She advises and counsels management on collective bargaining negotiations, grievance and arbitration proceedings, and jurisdictional disputes, and she represents companies in multiemployer bargaining and in federal and state courts. Wernick also advises on due diligence for unionized asset and stock transactions, including bargaining effects and mitigation of withdrawal liability.
In addition, Wernick counsels hotels and restaurants, nonprofit organizations, municipalities, and other public entities navigating labor issues across different legal frameworks. She was recognized in the 2026 edition of
The Best Lawyers in America
®
guide for Employment Law – Management and included as a Notable Leader in Employment and Labor Law by Crain’s Chicago Business in 2023. Wernick earned her J.D. from DePaul University College of Law and her B.A.,
cum laude
, from The Ohio State University.
“Christina, Megan, and Emily each add experience that our Chicago clients will benefit from right away,” said
Jennifer Colvin
, office managing shareholder in Chicago. “Collectively, they provide business leaders with a broad range of labor and employment support, handling everything from collective bargaining and prevailing wage matters to discrimination claims, which complements our team nicely and strengthens our service offering for employers across Illinois.”
“Employers need labor counsel who understands the realities of running their business, not just the impact of the law,” Wernick said. “Throughout my career, I’ve focused my practice on giving that kind of practical, hands-on guidance, whether at the bargaining table, on site, working through a labor dispute, or in the middle of a deal. My clients’ projects and workforces have never stopped at the Illinois border, and Ogletree Deakins’ national platform and deep labor bench create a tremendous opportunity to build on that work and continue delivering responsive, business-focused advice. I’m excited to join the firm alongside Megan and Emily, whose versatile skill sets will make an immediate impact for the team and our clients.”
Megan Wilkes has more than 12 years of experience representing management in grievance actions and prevailing wage matters. She interprets and negotiates collective bargaining agreements, including project labor agreements, analyzes jurisdictional disputes, and handles ERISA audit and collection actions. She also defends employers in civil litigation, including employment discrimination and retaliation claims. She earned her J.D. from the University of Illinois Chicago School of Law and her B.A. from DePaul University.
Emily Chramiec handles a wide variety of labor and employment law matters, with a focus on discrimination. She earned her J.D. from Chicago-Kent College of Law with a certificate in labor and employment law and her B.A. from Loyola University Chicago. While in law school, she was a member of the Moot Court Honor Society and a student editor for the Employee Rights & Employment Policy Journal, and she received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award in Employment Discrimination.
The Chicago team continues to grow strategically, as the office has added 11 lawyers this year already. This reflects a larger growth strategy at Ogletree Deakins, which welcomed more than 30 shareholders to the firm in 2026 across its international footprint.
About Ogletree Deakins
With more than 1,200 attorneys in 62 offices worldwide, Ogletree Deakins is one of the largest labor and employment law firms representing management. We handle all types of employment-related legal matters, including traditional labor and employment, workplace safety, employee benefits, and business immigration matters. Guided by our
Client Pledge
, we focus on understanding clients’ business and objectives, collaborating and anticipating needs, harnessing technology and innovation, communicating effectively, and providing quality representation with exceptional value.

# Pliant Raises $80 Million Series C to Open B2B Payment Infrastructure to AI Agents

*Seaya Nova and Speedinvest lead the oversubscribed round as Pliant opens its commercial payments infrastructure to a new generation of AI-powered payment infrastructure and accelerates expansion across North America*

**Berlin, November 4, 2026** – Pliant, a global fintech specializing in highly modular B2B payment solutions, today announced an $80 million Series C funding round led by Seaya Nova and Speedinvest, with participation from Illuminate Financial, Motive Partners and Molten Ventures. The investment will support Pliant’s continued expansion in the United States and Canada, prepare its entry into further international markets, and accelerate its AI roadmap as businesses connect AI agents directly to their financial infrastructure.

The funding follows three consecutive years in which Pliant has doubled its business and comes shortly after the company surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). Pliant employs more than 300 people across eight offices and processes billions of dollars in annual payment volume for businesses and partners across Europe and North America. Its customers span travel, insurance and AI-native companies, as well as banks, fintechs and software platforms building their own commercial payment offerings.

Pliant’s platform is built for a world in which AI increasingly runs business payments. The platform’s own AI agents help customers automate recurring finance work at scale. Third-party agents, from assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to a company's own AI automations, connect to Pliant via Model Context Protocol (MCP) and embed payment workflows into a wide range of business processes. The new capital will go toward deepening the company’s capabilities across agentic payments and workflows. 

“We built Pliant as an API-first, modular B2B payments platform from day one, and we have adopted AI deeply, in our product and in how we run the company,” said Malte Rau, CEO and co-founder of Pliant. “Whether an established business wants AI to automate its payment processes with the right guardrails, or an AI-native company needs a licensed partner that moves as fast as it does, Pliant is built for that. This investment will help us take that foundation further, opening more of our infrastructure directly to AI agents and expanding into new markets as we build the payment platform for the next generation of businesses.”

“Pliant has solved some of the most complex challenges in commercial payments, and as AI changes how companies move money, the licensed infrastructure underneath becomes more important, not less,” said Vinoth Jayakumar, General Partner at Seaya Nova. “Malte, Fabian and the team are positioned to be the payment partner of choice for this new generation of businesses, in Europe, North America and beyond.”  
  
**About Pliant**

Pliant is a modular B2B payments platform combining commercial card issuing, payment accounts, FX and spend management for businesses and AI agents.   
  
Businesses across travel, e-commerce, insurance and AI-native technology use Pliant to manage complex payment workflows, while fintechs, software platforms and banks use its infrastructure to build and operate their own commercial payment offerings. Pliant's API-first platform also enables AI agents and applications to access regulated payment infrastructure with permissions, controls and auditability built in.   
  
Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Berlin, Pliant serves businesses and partners across Europe and North America. A principal member of Visa and Mastercard, Pliant issues commercial cards in 13 currencies across 32 countries under its European e-money license and through regulated partners in the UK and US.   
  
Learn more at www.getpliant.com.

AXISCADES Purchases 90% Stake in Cloud Wave for ₹234 Crore to Grow Aerospace Manufacturing
AXISCADES completed the cash-funded buyout of a 90% stake in Cloud Wave Technologies and its subsidiaries on September 10, 2026. The transaction is valued at a purchase consideration of ₹234 crore, reflecting an enterprise valuation of approximately ₹260 crore. This acquisition provides AXISCADES with immediate, certified precision manufacturing capabilities to fuel its Power 930 roadmap.
Sahi Markets
Published:
11 Sept 2026, 11:41 AM IST (2 months ago)
Last Updated:
11 Sept 2026, 11:41 AM IST (2 months ago)
4 min read
Reviewed by
Arpit Seth
Share
Market snapshot:
AXISCADES Technologies Limited has executed transaction documents and completed the acquisition of a 90% stake in Bengaluru-based precision manufacturing firm Cloud Wave Technologies Private Limited for ₹234 crore. The transaction, completed on September 10, 2026, also hands AXISCADES a 90% indirect interest in Cloud Wave's wholly owned subsidiaries, Protohubs and Aureate. This strategic buyout accelerates AXISCADES' ongoing transition from an asset-light engineering services model into a specialized aerospace and defense manufacturing player.
Data Snapshot
AXISCADES acquired a 90% controlling interest in Cloud Wave Technologies for a cash consideration of ₹234 crore.
The transaction values Cloud Wave Technologies at an enterprise valuation of approximately ₹260 crore.
AXISCADES approved raising up to ₹200 crore via secured, unlisted, redeemable Non-Convertible Debentures at a coupon rate of 12.5% per annum to finance the deal.
AXISCADES reported a consolidated net loss of ₹14.83 crore for Q1 FY27, despite continuing operations revenue surging 94.17% YoY to ₹183.35 crore.
What's Changed
Prior to the transaction, AXISCADES operated primarily as an engineering design services business. Shifting into physical manufacturing via Cloud Wave adds immediate industrial capacity and AS9100D-certified aerospace operations.
Cloud Wave's audited turnover grew from ₹36.98 crore in FY24 to ₹68.25 crore in FY25, and reached ₹107.78 crore in FY26, highlighting a strong scaling trajectory (≈57.92% YoY growth in FY26) prior to being acquired.
AXISCADES' debt structure expands with a ₹200 crore high-coupon (12.5% p.a.) debt fundraise via unlisted NCDs to finance the cash-funded transaction.
Key Takeaways
AXISCADES completed the acquisition of a 90% controlling stake in Cloud Wave Technologies and its subsidiaries Protohubs and Aureate on September 10, 2026.
The buyout values Cloud Wave at an enterprise valuation of approximately ₹260 crore, leaving AXISCADES with an option to acquire the remaining 10% stake in a subsequent step.
To fund the cash-funded transaction, the board of AXISCADES approved raising up to ₹200 crore through high-yield 12.5% p.a. secured, unlisted NCDs.
The acquisition acts as a key building block for AXISCADES' 'Power 930' growth blueprint, supplementing its upcoming 240,000 sq ft Centre for Advanced Manufacturing in Bengaluru.
SAHI Perspective
The buyout of Cloud Wave is a defining milestone in AXISCADES' transition from an asset-light, effort-billed services organization to a proprietary products and manufacturing platform. Historically dependent on engineering services, AXISCADES is aggressively shifting into high-margin aerospace and defense manufacturing. By adding seven operational manufacturing units equipped with crucial AS9100D precision engineering certification, AXISCADES eliminates standard gestation lags. While the ₹200 crore NCD issuance at 12.5% coupon elevates the company's near-term debt burden, the ongoing ₹2,256 crore divestment of its legacy services unit to Akkodis provides a massive capital cushion to absorb transition costs and scale manufacturing operations.
Market Implications
This transaction strengthens AXISCADES' competitive positioning within India's rapidly expanding defense and aerospace manufacturing ecosystem. By integrating Cloud Wave's expertise in precision machining, sheet metal fabrication, and 3D printing, AXISCADES becomes a vertically integrated engineering-plus-manufacturing player. This directly qualifies the firm to bid for larger domestic programs with defense and aerospace agencies such as HAL, ADA, and DRDO, while deepening existing relationships with global OEM and Tier-1 customers.
Trading Signals
Market Bias:
Bullish
The successful execution and completion of the ₹234 crore Cloud Wave buyout positions AXISCADES to capture physical manufacturing margins. Bolstered by the ₹2,256 crore divestment of its legacy services business to Akkodis and a ₹200 crore NCD fundraise, the company's high-margin pivot is adequately capitalized.
Overweight:
Aerospace Manufacturing, Defence Engineering, Precision Machining
Trigger Factors:
Successful operational integration and cost synergies across Cloud Wave's seven manufacturing units.
Closing progress on the multi-tranche ₹2,256 crore divestment of the Aerospace Engineering Services business to Akkodis.
Commissioning timeline and OEM orders at the upcoming 240,000 sq ft Centre for Advanced Manufacturing (CAM) in Devanahalli.
Time Horizon:
Medium-term (3–12 months)
Industry Context
The Indian defense and aerospace manufacturing sector is witnessing an unprecedented push, driven by aggressive domestic sourcing policies and global OEM supply chain diversification. Precision components are highly sought after in aerospace and semiconductor manufacturing. AXISCADES' entry via Cloud Wave, which was founded in 2014 and has matured its capability across seven manufacturing units, positions it alongside domestic peers such as Azad Engineering and Aequs to capture both local and export demand.
Key Risks to Watch
Operational integration risks stemming from coordinating and managing Cloud Wave's seven manufacturing units.
Near-term debt-servicing pressure from the high-yield ₹200 crore unlisted NCDs carrying a 12.5% p.a. coupon.
Temporary profitability drag during the business model transition, as evidenced by the consolidated net loss of ₹14.83 crore reported in Q1 FY27 due to overlapping overheads.
Recent Developments
On September 11, 2026, AXISCADES announced the completion of its 90% acquisition of Cloud Wave Technologies and its subsidiaries on September 10, 2026. Prior to this, on September 5, 2026, the board approved raising ₹200 crore via NCDs to fund the deal. In its Q1 FY27 earnings released on August 13, 2026, AXISCADES reported a 94.17% YoY increase in continuing operations revenue to ₹183.35 crore, though transitional outlays led to a net loss of ₹14.83 crore. In corporate actions, promoter Jupiter Capital sold 10 lakh shares (2.35% stake) for ₹166.77 crore on June 30, 2026, trimming its voting stake to 50.15%. Additionally, in June 2026, AXISCADES agreed to divest its Aerospace Engineering Services business to Akkodis for ₹2,256 crore.
Closing Insight
AXISCADES is orchestrating a classic corporate transformation, exchanging its asset-light design services business for an active, certified manufacturing engine. By bypassing organic build-out times through this targeted ₹234 crore acquisition, the company is directly capitalizing on India's aerospace and defense manufacturing tailwinds.
